Matter is taken up in the revised call.

By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
12 of 2024 at Police Station Anoopshahar, District Bulandshahar under Sections 366, 376, 328, 506 I.P.C.
The applicant is in jail since 08.07.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 19.01.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Akhilesh Chandra Shukla, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Ms. Sandhya Singh, learned counsel on behalf of the informant and Shri Suchit Tandon, learned AGA from the record, entitle the applicant for Deepak Chaudhary vs State Of U.P. on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21191185/
1 grant of bail:
1. The victim and the applicant were intimate and had consensual physical relations.
2. The FIR is a result of the said relationship between the victim and the applicant going awry.
3. False and aggravated allegations were made in the FIR to implicate the entire family of the applicant including his sister-in-law and brother-in-law.
4. The criminal case is being leveraged to extort money from the applicant.
5. The victim in her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.

sentences.text: In the meantime she got engaged to be married to a third person but her videos had been circulated to her in laws and her friends.
Lastly, she has stated that her mother had shown her the indecent videos.
6. The applicant never transmitted any indecent photograph of the victim.
The same photographs were captured by both the parties during subsistence of their relationship.
However, they merely depict intimacy and are not indecent.
7. The applicant never captured any indecent videos or circulated the same.
The investigations have contradicted the prosecution case.
8. No indecent videos have been recovered from the mobile of the applicant nor there is any evidence to establish circulation of such videos.
9. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
In fact the victim did not undergo medical examination.

10. Major inconsistencies in the FIR, the statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
discredit the prosecution case.
11. The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
12. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
13. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.

sentences.text: In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Deepak Chaudhary be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

(iii) The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru.
Prin. Secy. Home Deptt. (Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
